title: Reject chains of infix after/before connectors
defect: 'A after B before C', 'A before B after C' and similar chains are outside the documented grammar (a group holds exactly two clauses) but were accepted: the held-out run (seed 20260601) accepted all 300 ambiguous cases.
hypothesis: Marking a row that was opened by an infix after/before connector (GRP) and flagging a second infix after/before that arrives while the current row carries GRP will reject exactly the chained constructions, without touching prefix forms ('after A, B') or groups separated by then/and/full stop.
affected: row field GRP (new, marker); B units w_GRP_after, w_GRP_before, err_chained_after, err_chained_before.
mathematical_effect: GRP_{p'} += relu(adv + x_AFTER - 1) (and the same for BEFORE): 1 on the new row iff the boundary was caused by an infix connector. err_chained_after = relu(x_AFTER + hasACT(r) + GRP(r) - 2) is 1 only when all three conditions hold, adding 1 to the sticky error mass (threshold 0.5).
expected: All chained cases in tests/next/defects-002.jsonl are rejected; dev set and patch-001 targets unchanged.
